# BINDING CONSISTENCY LEDGER — French Listening Pod (15 scenes)

## 1. TRANSLITERATION
Not needed — names stay as written.

## 2. PRICES

£8.40 → huit euros quarante
£12.50 → douze euros cinquante
£4 (implied: pint) → quatre euros cinquante
£3 (implied: half-pint) → trois euros
£5 (implied: glass wine) → cinq euros
£2 (implied: glass wine) → deux euros cinquante

## 3. TARGET-LANGUAGE NAME
Le français

## 4. RECURRING LINES

| Canonical | French rendering |
|-----------|------------------|
| Good morning. What can I get you? | Bonjour ! Qu'est-ce que je peux vous proposer ? |
| Good afternoon. What can I get you? | Bon après-midi. Qu'est-ce que je peux vous proposer ? |
| Good evening. What can I get you? | Bonsoir. Qu'est-ce que je peux vous proposer ? |
| Would you like to sit-in or takeaway? | Vous préférez sur place ou à emporter ? |
| Could I pay by card? | Je peux payer par carte ? |
| Do you have contactless? | Vous avez le sans-contact ? |
| Thank you very much. Goodbye. | Merci beaucoup. Au revoir. |
| Excuse me. | Excusez-moi. |
| Yes, of course. | Oui, bien sûr. |
| I'm learning French. | J'apprends le français. |
| You speak very good French. | Vous parlez très bien le français. |
| That's very kind of you. | C'est très gentil de votre part. |
| Thank you very much. | Merci beaucoup. |

## 5. REGISTER

**Customer ↔ Service staff** (café, pub, restaurant, shop, hotel, chemist, taxi): **vous** throughout. Openings with no pronoun (*Bonjour !*, *Bonsoir !*); requests anchored to *s'il vous plaît* and *merci*.

**Strangers meeting for the first time** (tourist ↔ local, passenger ↔ passenger, learner ↔ friend on first encounter): **vous** on first contact; can soften to **tu** if rapport is established mid-scene, but open with **vous**.

**Peers / established friends**: **tu** (Scenes 4, 15: friend contexts, ongoing conversation).

**Neighbours**: **vous** (formal register, early morning/evening greetings).
